question: Sally and Jerome Poncet are residents on an archipelago located how far from South America's southern Patagonian coast ?

results.title: Damien Bay
results.text: Damien Bay ( ) is located north-northeast of Hamilton Bay on the southeast coast of South Georgia. It was named after the yacht "Damien II", owned by Sally and Jerome Poncet, residents of Beaver Island in the Falkland Islands. The Poncets conducted investigations of the breeding colonies of seals and seabirds around the coastline of South Georgia. The "Damien II" was chartered by the British Antarctic Survey for various wildlife surveys between 1985 and 1992.

results.title: Sally Prouty
results.text: Sally Prouty (born Sarah Green) (December 23, 1922 - September 7, 2014) was an American retired table tennis champion. She was inducted into the United States of America Table Tennis (USATT) Hall of Fame in 1979.

results.title: Sally, Irene and Mary (1938 film)
results.text: Sally, Irene and Mary is a 1938 American comedy film directed by William A. Seiter and written by Harry Tugend and Jack Yellen. The film stars Alice Faye, Tony Martin, Fred Allen, Joan Davis, Marjorie Weaver and Gregory Ratoff. The film was released on March 4, 1938, by 20th Century Fox.

results.title: Falkland Islands
results.text: The Falkland Islands ( ; Spanish: "Islas Malvinas" , ] ) are an archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean on the Patagonian Shelf. The principal islands are about 300 mi east of South America's southern Patagonian coast, at a latitude of about 52°S. The archipelago, with an area of 4700 sqmi , comprises East Falkland, West Falkland and 776 smaller islands. As a British overseas territory, the Falklands have internal self-governance, and the United Kingdom takes responsibility for their defence and foreign affairs. The islands' capital is Stanley on East Falkland.

results.title: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
results.text: The Southern Patagonian Ice Field (Spanish: "Hielo Continental" or "Campo de Hielo Sur" ), located at the Southern Patagonic Andes between Chile and Argentina, is the world's second largest contiguous extrapolar ice field. It is the bigger of two remnant parts of the Patagonian Ice Sheet, which covered all of southern Chile during the last glacial period, locally called the Llanquihue glaciation.
